[USER] The user got into a heated discussion on Reddit about the impact of social media on relationships last month.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided an overview of research on the impact of social media on relationships, summarizing key findings.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Positive effects of social media on relationships include increased connectivity, social support, and relationship maintenance.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Negative effects of social media on relationships include social comparison, decreased face-to-face interaction, misinterpretation and misunderstandings, and Facebook depression.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant cited sources for positive effects: Pew Research Center (2019), Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology (2015), Computers in Human Behavior (2015).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant cited sources for negative effects: Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin (2013), Psychology of Popular Media Culture (2017), Journal of Language and Social Psychology (2015), Cyberpsychology, Behavior, and Social Networking (2015).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other findings include the importance of relationship quality over quantity, individual differences in personality traits, and the influence of context on social media use.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Notable studies and researchers mentioned include Pew Research Center, Dr. Jean Twenge, and Dr. Sherry Turkle.  
[USER] The user is particularly interested in the negative effects of social media on relationships.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant elaborated on "Facebook depression," describing it as feelings of depression, anxiety, and loneliness triggered by social media use.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Causes of Facebook depression include social comparison, unrealistic expectations, fear of missing out (FOMO), lack of real-life social connections, and sleep disturbances.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained how Facebook depression affects romantic relationships, friendships, family relationships, and self-comparison.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided suggestions to mitigate Facebook depression, including setting boundaries, practicing self-compassion, focusing on real-life connections, taking breaks from social media, and seeking professional help.  
[USER] The user has experienced feelings of inadequacy when seeing others post about their fancy vacations or new cars.  
[USER] The user asked whether social media companies have a responsibility to address negative effects or if it is up to individuals to be more mindful.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant discussed the responsibility of social media companies, including design changes, algorithmic transparency, providing mental health resources, content moderation, and collaboration with researchers.
